source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:16 (the Masorah's three-defective list)
claim_en: u-shfachot ('and maidservants') written DEFECTIVE (no second vav) — three in the Torah, the Masorah's mnemonic: 'to Abram he did good' (12:16), 'Avimelech took' (20:14), 'the LORD blessed my master' (24:35). The Hilleli copy reads plene here; SNAPSHOT sides with the Yerushalmi codex and the Masorah: defective at exactly the three.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:16 (the book-splitting Masorah)
claim_en: The rule's boundary: 'from the book's beginning until THE MAN BURST FORTH (30:43) the maidservant-plural is written defective; from there to the Torah's end, always plene.' The first plene token is the boundary verse itself.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:16 (the book-splitting Masorah)
claim_en: The rule's far side: every remaining maidservant-plural token (Jacob's camp-ordering, 33:1/2/6) is plene — the book-splitting rule holds END-TO-END on SNAPSHOT: three defective before the boundary, four plene at and after it, nothing else anywhere in the Torah.

va-yehallelu ('and they PRAISED her') — 'the first lamed is LIGHT, to ease the tongue, like va-etpalela in Daniel 9:4.' SNAPSHOT: the doubling dot is absent from the first lamed — the praise-hapax's very form is a lightened one; the Daniel pair rides as an edge.

yechayu ('they will KEEP ALIVE') — two in the Masorah: here and 'they shall revive as the grain' (Hosea 14:8). Torah-side: exactly ONE token — the fear-verse's life-verb is unique in the Torah; the Hosea leg rides as an edge.

achoti at ('you are my sister') — two in the Masorah: here and 'say to wisdom: you are my sister' (Prov 7:4) — 'Abraham and Sarah were great in wisdom.' Torah-side: the two-word pair stands exactly once (12:13; every other 'my sister' token is followed by another word). The Proverbs leg — a SAY-command aimed at the sister-word, like Abram's own imri — rides as an edge.

qach va-lekh ('TAKE and GO') — the Masorah's five-member hand-to-hand list (the Kitzur: what is given passes from hand to hand — so Pharaoh surely gave gifts here too). Torah-side: the pair stands exactly TWICE — Pharaoh releasing Sarai (12:19) and Laban's house releasing Rivkah (24:51): both wife-transfer releases; the Kings and Jeremiah legs ride as edges.

THE PAVED-WAY MACHINE: THIS EPISODE IS READ AS A SPECIFICATION THE NATION LATER EXECUTES. 'Go and pave the way before your descendants' - and the chain lists ELEVEN matched ink-pairs between this descent and Israel's, word answering word: famine and famine, descended and descended, to-sojourn and to-sojourn, severe and severe. The unit is thereby not merely a precedent but a template whose tokens are checked one by one against the later text. Its pairs return as credited seats across the rest of Genesis.

check.note: An episode read as a token-by-token template for a later national event, with eleven matched ink-pairs enumerated.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 41:2; Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 7:9:3; Vayikra Rabbah 16:1; Arakhin 16a:9
claim_en: THE AFFLICTION OF OUR 12:17 IS IDENTIFIED AS A NAMED DISEASE AND CARRIED INTO LIVE DIVORCE LAW. The affliction is identified as the one condition that blocks marital relations - the measure exactly matching the crime - and that identification is quoted inside the halakhic sugya on conditions that compel a divorce, with an attribution variance recorded. Two further cause-claims ride the same verse: forbidden relations at one Babylonian seat, and the inciting of discord between husband and wife at another, where the count of the census is itself disputed.

check.note: An affliction operator identified with a named condition, that identification then quoted inside a live divorce-law discussion.

claim_en: A MEASURE-FOR-MEASURE ARITHMETIC IS COMPUTED ON OUR 12:20. Because Pharaoh escorted the departing household - 'and he commanded men concerning him' - for FOUR STEPS, he was repaid with four hundred years of his descendants' service. The escort law's standing rules are stated beside it. A courtesy in this unit is priced, and the price is paid in the decree of a later unit.

check.note: A small act in this unit converted into an exact numeric obligation discharged in a later one.

claim_en: A UNIQUENESS CLAIM IS MADE ON OUR EXIT VERSE. 'No slave or maidservant ever went free from Egypt EXCEPT HAGAR' - proved from our 12:20, 'and they sent him away, him and his wife and all that was his'. The verse's inventory clause is read as covering a person the narrative has not yet named, seating Hagar's origin in this episode.

check.note: An inventory clause read as covering an unnamed person, seating a later character's origin in this unit.

claim_en: A GRAMMAR RULE THE PARSE LAYER ALREADY ENCODES IS STATED AS LAW AT ITS HALAKHIC SEAT. R. Nechemya's rule - a word that would take a directing prefix at its start instead takes a HEH at its end - is stated in the legal discussion, and the school of Rabbi Yishmael's census of that form includes our 12:10's own directional token. The morphology this unit records mechanically is here a named, cited rule.

check.note: A morphological pattern the unit already encodes, stated as a named rule at a legal seat with this unit's token in its census.

claim_en: TWO READINGS PRICED ON SINGLE PARTICLES. The request particle at our 12:13 is read as making the plan SOLICITED rather than imposed - set in explicit contrast with the later Gerar episode, where he said it of her by force. And the intensifier at our 12:14 is graded against its use elsewhere: where another woman is 'fair UP TO' the intensifier, meaning not including it, Sarah is described by the intensifier itself - so 'she did not reach half of Sarah's beauty'. An exclusive-particle parse used as a comparative measure.

check.note: A request particle read as establishing consent, and an intensifier graded by an exclusive-particle parse against another verse.
